feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear progression, relevant senior-level scope, and a consistent focus on digital communications strategy. It reads professionally and is well targeted, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consultant roles, which supports credibility and leadership growth.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are presented clearly and consistently.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds substance and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/activity: e.g., engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads a bit generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding clearer seniority/sector context would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Add public-sector/association context to reflect the strongest through-line in the experience section.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, evidence-aligned positioning tied to digital transformation, governance, and content operations.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, digital governance, and content operations that improve coordination across complex teams. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also reappear in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Editorial systems & governance” instead of “Editorial workflow design.”
- Group related items and remove softer phrasing: “Stakeholder coordination” and “cross-department coordination” can become “Cross-functional leadership & stakeholder alignment.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles: include “CMS modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “advocacy communications.”
- Suggested version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics infrastructure & reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional leadership & stakeholder alignment • Public-sector policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant scope, senior advisory value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with positioning: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits.”
- Rephrase technical work to show business value: “Improved web operations through CMS enhancements, front-end fixes, analytics workflows, and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/discovery gains, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this item focused on advisory/consulting contributions since Oct. 2024.
- Microsite and AI search language duplicates Recent Projects; reference them more briefly here unless you add outcomes not mentioned elsewhere.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like, bullets started with outcomes, and channel-management points were tightened to avoid overlap with the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading team operations, platform strategy, analytics, governance and budget across web, email, social and video.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable results if available: email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Combine infrastructure/operations bullets if space is tight: “Built NACo’s analytics and governance stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership, modernization and systems.
- Video production language also appears in older roles; emphasize building the in-house studio and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as broad responsibility than distinct impact. Tighten it to emphasize what changed or grew under your leadership at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging during a period of channel growth.”
- Make bullets outcome-led and parallel: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet to show creation/adoption: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating channel ownership language.
- “Produced weekly video updates” also appears in the prior role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not just producing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications systems leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Prefer “communications systems” or “content operations” over “messaging,” which reads less senior and duplicates experience bullets.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header summary and multiple NACo experience entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, higher-value capabilities: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress unless it is important for target roles; recent experience is overwhelmingly Drupal-led.
- Replace “Power Pages” and possibly “SharePoint” here if they are not central to recent achievements; keep them in “Technical + IT” instead.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences” or “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; use topline skills for strategic themes, not full platform inventory.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating too many identical phrases.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, content performance and conversion analysis”
- Lead with capability, then tools; this better matches the seniority shown in recent roles.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive/leadership dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., improved reporting cadence, adoption, or decision-making speed).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

- Consider keeping Topline Skills strategic and leaving the full tool stack to Technical + IT.

Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and technical breadth without repeating basic video terms.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating skills already evidenced in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize recency/strength: put **Drupal** first and consider adding a qualifier like **advanced** or **primary platform**.
- Keep only platforms here; leave modernization, front-end, APIs, and automation in the adjacent technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry almost exactly; consider merging or removing one.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus of the rest of the CV unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group operational tools separately for clarity: “Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add one brief qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal-based sites, campaign microsites, and workflow automation”
- Consider trimming older/basic terms if space is tight; keep the strongest differentiators: API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, GTM

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version high-level and make this one more tool-specific
- “Google Tag Manager” may also fit better under analytics/measurement if you need to reduce overlap here

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two tighter groups to show intent: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and “Work management/collaboration: Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.”
- Cut lower-value or older/generic tools unless they are current and used recently; Basecamp and Trello are the best removal candidates.
- Rename the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent systems/governance work.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier instead of more tools, e.g. “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them too prominently in multiple sections.
- Slack and Teams are standard collaboration tools; keep only if they support ATS coverage or current-role relevance.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the strategic/enterprise angle shown elsewhere. It should signal scale and platform ownership without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use, e.g. **enterprise email automation, member communications, campaign journeys**
- Keep it platform-focused rather than outcome-focused here; save audience size/newsletter volume for the NACo roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that is already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so a more specific label will reduce vagueness.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to highlight hands-on delivery and light supervision: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”
- If metrics exist, replace “high-impact” with specifics: “produced X livestreams/year,” “launched weekly video series,” or “improved publishing speed/consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and use stronger action verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific output if possible (e.g., web features, audio segments, campaign materials).
- If available, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the content supported advocacy/program visibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia production; later roles already cover video, digital content and channel operations in much stronger detail.
- Don’t repeat “first” team-building or digital function claims here unless this role truly introduced podcasting specifically.
